_comment: Every MLIR dialect answers for itself: taught by a chapter, referenced in passing, planned with the slice that closes it, or declared out of scope with a reason. Checked by tools/verify-mlir-coverage.py against reference/mlir-surface-23.json.

acc.reason: OpenACC as an offload programming model. The corpus teaches the IR a frontend produces, not the source-level pragma dialects that produce it; the same boundary excludes OpenMP.

amdgpu.reason: A target backend dialect: its operations are a one-to-one spelling of that vendor's intrinsics. The corpus teaches target-specific code through LLVM's intrinsic surface in 13-advanced-ir/02-target-specific-intrinsics.md and the porting map in 12-backend-jit/, which is the mechanism; enumerating one vendor's operation list would date with that vendor's hardware and duplicate upstream reference material.

async.reason: A task-parallel execution model. The corpus's concurrency material is about atomics and memory ordering at the IR level (04-memory), which is a different subject from a coroutine-shaped task dialect.

dlti.reason: Data layout and target information, carried entirely as attributes: this dialect ships zero operations, which is why it appears in the misalignment table below. The layout facts it holds are taught as LLVM data layout in 02-types.

emitc.slice: 2.2 compiler dialects: MLIR emitting C, the mirror image of the C-to-IR direction 20-clang-frontend teaches

gpu.slice: 2.3 ML dialects: the host/device split, and where nvvm and rocdl become reachable through one portable layer

irdl.slice: 2.2 compiler dialects: 22-bcir-approach/04-dialect-as-data.md already projects BCIR into IRDL but names none of the dialect's own 17 operations

linalg.slice: 2.3 ML dialects: linalg is where tensor algebra becomes loops, and the corpus names exactly one of its 99 operations today

ml_program.reason: A container dialect for whole-program ML state. It has 11 operations and effectively no adoption outside its own tests; teaching it would date faster than anything else in this table.

mpi.reason: Message passing between processes, which is a distributed-systems subject rather than a compiler one. BCIR's own distributed backends are honest stubs, so there is nothing here to correspond to either.

omp.reason: OpenMP as a source-level programming model, excluded on the same boundary as OpenACC. Where OpenMP reaches IR the corpus does teach it, as the outlining and runtime-call shape in 20-clang-frontend.

pdl.slice: 2.2 compiler dialects: rewrite patterns as data, the same move 22-bcir-approach/04-dialect-as-data.md makes for op definitions

pdl_interp.slice: 2.2 compiler dialects: the matcher pdl compiles into, worth one section for the same reason a bytecode is worth teaching

ptr.reason: A low-level pointer dialect still being factored out of the LLVM dialect upstream. Teaching it now would teach a migration in progress; the pointer semantics a reader needs are in 02-types and 23-version-movement/02-ptrtoaddr.md.

quant.slice: 2.3 ML dialects: three operations, and the direct counterpart to BCIRQ8's quantization rule

shape.slice: 2.2 compiler dialects: shape as first-class IR, which is the prerequisite for reading linalg and tosa honestly

shard.reason: Tensor sharding for multi-device execution. In scope for a future distributed phase, but not reachable from anything the corpus teaches today, and BCIR's distributed rail is a stub.

smt.reason: An SMT-solver interface dialect. Formal verification of IR is a real subject and a legitimate future phase, but it is not compilation, and nothing else in the corpus depends on it.

sparse_tensor.slice: 2.3 ML dialects: sparsity as a type property rather than a loop structure, which is the idea BCIR's cost model needs to price

misalignments.vcix: The generated headers ship two vcix operations but this mlir-opt does not register the dialect: it is built for RISC-V vendor co-processor extensions and is not in the default registration set. Headers and registry disagreeing is normal for a vendor dialect and is recorded here so the gate does not report it as an extraction failure.
misalignments.dlti: Registered with zero operations, which is correct rather than broken: DLTI models data layout and target information as attributes and types only. It is the anti-vacuity canary for this gate -- an extraction bug that silently returned no operations would look exactly like DLTI, so DLTI is the one dialect allowed to look like that, by name.
